definition: TOD (Transfer-on-death) refers to named beneficiaries receiving assets at the death of the property owner without the need for probate, facilitating the executor's disposition of the property owner's assets after his or her death. This is often accomplished through a TOD deed. The beneficiary of the TOD may be an individual or an organization, such as a charity. Alternate or successor beneficiaries can also be named in case the first beneficiary dies. Beneficiaries of the TOD do not have access to assets until the asset owner dies. The Uniform Transfer-on-Death Securities Registration Act provides that owners may designate beneficiaries for their stock, bond or brokerage accounts. In some states, vehicles, real estate can also be transferred by TOD.
